recentItems.title: UN probe finds grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran
recentItems.description:
A new UN investigation says there are reasonable grounds to believe the United States committed war crimes in two air strikes on civilian sites in Iran in February, while also finding that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity during a crackdown on nationwide protests that began in December 2025. The UN mission said a US air strike on a school in Minab killed more than 150 people, most of them children, and found no evidence that the school was being used for military purposes. It reached a similar conclusion about a US air strike on a sports centre in Lamerd that killed and injured 22 civilians. The US Department of Defense says it is investigating the incidents. The investigation also accused Iranian authorities of unlawful killings, torture, persecution and other abuses during the protest crackdown. Iranian authorities say 3,117 people were killed and have attributed most of the deaths to civilians and security personnel killed by what they describe as rioters backed by foreign powers. UN investigators say the actual death toll is likely to be significantly higher, while rights groups have reported substantially higher figures, although the numbers remain difficult to verify amid an extended internet shutdown. 

Al Jazeera's Sinem Koseoglu reports from Tehran.

recentItems.title: Makeshift Gaza clinic helps war-wounded recover despite prosthetic shortages
recentItems.description:
Thousands of Palestinians in Gaza have suffered life-changing injuries during the war, with children among those most affected. The World Health Organisation says one in four people injured in Gaza since October 2023 has sustained a life-changing injury, with children accounting for up to a quarter of those cases, or around 10,000 children. With medical supplies, prosthetic materials and specialist care in short supply, only about 500 people have received permanent prosthetics. In Khan Younis, a makeshift tent clinic is repairing damaged prostheses and providing temporary support to Palestinians who have struggled to find treatment elsewhere. Prosthetics technician Mohammed al-Khaldi says they repair damaged devices so patients can continue living in difficult conditions inside displacement camps. For many patients, including children, rehabilitation is about more than restoring mobility; it offers hope and a way to rebuild their lives after devastating injuries. 

Al Jazeera's Nargess Moballeghi reports from Gaza.

recentItems.title: Yemen’s Houthis and Iran: How deep is their alliance?
recentItems.description:
Yemen’s Houthi movement has expanded its reach along the western coast, striking Saudi energy infrastructure while Riyadh responds with airstrikes. Analysts say the group, rooted in a 1990s Zaydi revival, shares ties with Iran but retains independent Yemeni origins. UN experts have documented support from Iran’s Revolutionary Guards and Hezbollah, though Tehran denies arming the Houthis. Control over Hodeidah and key waterways like Bab al-Mandeb underscores the wider regional and global trade stakes at play.

Al Jazeera’s Ali Hashem reports.

recentItems.title: Syrian court sentences three over 2025 coastal mass killings
recentItems.description:
A Syrian military criminal court has sentenced three men over their roles in mass killings along Syria’s coast in March 2025, in the first major test of the new government’s efforts to hold perpetrators accountable for the violence. Two of those sentenced were affiliated with the former Bashar al-Assad regime, while the third was linked to government forces; a fourth defendant was acquitted for lack of evidence. One former regime loyalist received a life sentence for looting and involvement in an illegal armed group, while another was sentenced to death for killing two people and given a life sentence for other offences including looting and inciting violence. A fighter affiliated with government forces received a 20-year sentence for murder. The violence began with fighting between former regime-affiliated fighters and government security forces on March 6, 2025, and escalated into mass killings in which more than 1,400 people were killed, most of them Alawite civilians, according to the UN, rights groups and the government’s own investigation. The trials began in November 2025 following a government investigation, with more verdicts expected. 

Al Jazeera’s Obeida Hitto reports from Aleppo.
